Perfect! After **Kc2**, Black has **Nxa1+** (check!), and after **Ke2**, Black still plays **Nxa1** winning the rook. All king moves lose the rook. **Nb3+** is the winning move—it's a fork that wins the undefended rook on a1, and since the knight gives check, White must move the king, allowing Black to capture the rook cleanly.

**Best move:** Nb3+

**Main line:** 1...Nb3+ 2.Ke3 Nxa1 (or 2.Kc2 Nxa1+; 2.Ke2 Nxa1; 2.Kd3 Nxa1; all lose the rook)

**Motif:** fork

**Coaching note:**
A knight fork with check is one of the most powerful tactics. Your knight on c5 attacked the undefended rook on a1, but only when you gave check with Nb3+. White's king had to move, leaving you free to collect the rook. Watch for undefended pieces the opponent has—a check can force their hand and let you capture material afterward.
